meta.label: Average annual rainfall (2015-2024)
meta.methodNote: Mean total annual precipitation, averaged across 2015-2024 (same ten-baseline-year departure from the WMO 30-year normal as the temperature layers, for the same CDS cost-cap reason; see scripts/etl/era5.py's own docstring). Built from the raw hourly ERA5-Land dataset (reanalysis-era5-land), not the derived daily-statistics dataset used for temperature above — that derived dataset excludes accumulated variables like precipitation from its own catalog entirely. Each day's total is read directly from the single 00:00 UTC reading on the FOLLOWING calendar day: ERA5-Land resets its accumulated fields at 00 UTC daily (unlike full ERA5, which resets at the 06/18 UTC forecast-run boundaries), so that one timestep already holds the whole day's accumulation — no hour-by-hour de-accumulation is performed. Confirmed against ECMWF's own support forum, checked live 2026-09-28. A 'day' here is a UTC calendar day (00-00 UTC), not the temperature layers' UTC+01:00 local day — immaterial to an annual total, but a real difference from how this file's own temperature layers define a day.
meta.coverageNote: ERA5-Land's native grid is ~9km (0.1 degree) resolution — each comune's figure is the nearest grid cell to its centroid, so comuni closer together than ~9km can show an identical figure. Mountain microclimates (a valley floor vs. the ridge above it) narrower than one grid cell are not distinguishable at this resolution. ERA5-Land excludes ocean cells entirely (no reading, not a real zero), so 226 comuni whose nearest grid cell falls over open sea (mostly narrow coastal strips, e.g. the Ligurian Riviera) are assigned the nearest LAND cell instead — a real ERA5-Land reading, just from a cell slightly further away, rather than a dropped or fabricated figure. One comune (024129, the merged 'Castegnero Nanto') has no centroid in the spine and is absent here rather than estimated. 1 comune(s) — 084020 — are small/remote enough that no ERA5-Land land cell exists within reach; using a distant mainland cell instead would misrepresent their climate, so they are absent here too, not force-matched.
